<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**12** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `97c0e57e0497256db6f36da3c55bb6c5bbc33c6f` — the merge of head `883af46685e88741f55ac36c67cad2c8159dcbd6` into base `c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 97c0e57e0497256db6f36da3c55bb6c5bbc33c6f && git checkout 97c0e57e0497256db6f36da3c55bb6c5bbc33c6f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1 883af46685e88741f55ac36c67cad2c8159dcbd6 && git checkout -B drift-repro c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1 && git merge --no-ff 883af46685e88741f55ac36c67cad2c8159dcbd6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c81f498b5f0614157864d9586da718dbe02121b1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T16:13Z

Head-sha: 14bb661513aeab3dda0fa988250a905f704362da
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34763 (claim 6951477440; os-dev report 6952850821). This is the executor half of #34828's `candidates` shape.

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #34763`. No other issue sits next to a closing verb. The body names #34868 as the carrier for the skill's one-near-form row.

**Scope vs claim.** Every path sits inside the claim:
- `packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-term-matcher.ts` (`findDatasetTermCandidates`) and `dataset-tools.ts`;
- `LIST_DATASETS_DESCRIPTION` and `DATASET_SELECTION_RULE` (`mcp-server-runtime.ts`);
- `packages/mcp/README.md` and `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`;
- the `ai.json` checklist (rev 3);
- tests and one changeset.

**Declaration.** `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`, and they agree. The shape was published by #34828 at `minor`; this PR fills it, so `@objectstack/service-analytics` and `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch` are right.

**Governed / size.** NOT governed, 494 lines.

**Check-runs at 14bb6615.** 59 runs, every one `success` or `skipped`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` and all 10 shards, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Live E2E UI`.

**Against ADR-0149 D3 and its note (#34828).**
- Exact match stays the only hit. A term with any hit (`matchedOn`) gets no candidates.
- A near form is containment either way after `normalizeDatasetTerm`, with a floor of `DATASET_TERM_NEAR_MIN_CODE_POINTS = 2`.
- Candidates are offered, never selected. `DATASET_SELECTION_RULE` now says to ask about candidates (one or many), not to treat any as a match, and to fall back to rule 4 only when there are none. That is the note's reading, which the seat ruled outranks #34792 Q1 A.
- `candidates` is set only when non-empty, so `.min(1)` holds.

**#34828 N2's four executor invariants.** All four are pinned:
- the cap: 5 per term with `break scan`, and the ablation takes a sixth entry;
- every `{dataset, member}` points at an entry listed in the same answer (`listed` is built from admitted members);
- a matched term has no candidate;
- order: measures before dimensions, in listing order.

**Tests and live run.** 6 matcher, 4 tools and 3 MCP cases (`list-datasets-candidates-34763.test.ts`), two ablations. The live showcase run gives `invoice` → `invoice_count`, `paid_count`.

**Docblock.** The `DATASET_SELECTION_RULE` docblock is left alone so this PR and #34881 merge cleanly (`overlap-check` exit 0 at `14bb6615`). #34881's rewrite of it points at the skill, which is still right after this lands.

**Tool text sizes.** `LIST_DATASETS_DESCRIPTION` 1095 → 1414 bytes, `DATASET_SELECTION_RULE` 453 → 741 bytes. Acceptable for the rule they now carry.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. A term sent twice is offered once (pinned), but the dedupe keys on the raw term, so `Invoice` and `invoice` in one call each get their own list (the same entries twice). Harmless, since the agent asks once, but keying on the normalized term would match how hits are judged. Not owed.
- N2. A term equal to a member the caller may not see (`membersWithheld`) can still get visible near candidates. That leaks nothing, since only admitted members are offered and the withheld count was already shown, but the agent may ask about a near form when the exact one exists and is withheld. Worth one line in #34868's skill row if it comes up. Not owed.
- N3. The 2-code-point containment floor is broad on short ASCII terms (`id`, `no` match many members). The cap of 5 bounds it, and over-offering is an extra question, never a wrong answer. Revisit only if a round shows noise.
- N4. Between this landing and #34868 landing, the served skill (from #34881) and these tool texts disagree on a single candidate: the tool says ask, the skill row may still read it otherwise. Land #34868 close behind.

Next: o3-E folds the MCP pin into `mcp-dataset-tools.test.ts` after #34881 merges. That push owes an L1-c delta read at the final head before landing. No seat L2 is owed.

## L1: ACCEPT (delta, final head) · 2026-11-17T19:03Z

Head-sha: 883af46685e88741f55ac36c67cad2c8159dcbd6
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c. This is a delta read of `14bb6615`..`883af466` against my 6953727363, the final-head read I owed after the MCP pin fold (os-dev report 6957909999).

### 席位核对

**Delta.** Two first-parent commits:
- `762b721b` is a merge of `main` at `c81f498b`, which includes #34881 (`c6ecd1fa`). Its first parent is my ACCEPTed head. The patch-id of the PR's diff from the merge-base to `14bb6615` equals the patch-id of the diff from `c81f498b` to `762b721b`, so the merge adds nothing and resolved no conflicts.
- `883af466` touches four paths, +85/-119:
  - **The pin fold.** `list-datasets-candidates-34763.test.ts` is deleted, and its three cases become a top-level `describe('[#34763] …')` in `mcp-dataset-tools.test.ts`, using that harness's own bridge and call helper. The cases are the same: the fixtures parse under `ListDatasetsOutputSchema`; candidates pass through with the same entries, in the same order and with nothing added; an answer without the key comes back without it. They assert the same things (the bridge-call assertion now reads the harness's `calls` log). This follows the AGENTS.md ruling 6583487846 the body cites.
  - **The checklist.** `ai.json` `automated.ref` drops the deleted file and keeps the others.
  - **The docblock.** The `DATASET_SELECTION_RULE` docblock now describes the candidates row (ask even for a single candidate, never a pick and never a match, and fall back only with no match and no candidate) and the two-metrics row. The rule string itself is byte-unchanged. That is the right place for it now that #34881 has landed the rewrite this PR had avoided touching.

**Gates.** Not governed, 468 lines. CI at the report: 40 success, none failed, with two re-runs pending after a body edit. This verdict holds on the condition that `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` finish green on this head.

**My earlier notes.** N1 to N3 stand as they were (none were owed). N4, the window in which the served skill text says "one near form selects nothing" while the tool texts ask on any candidate, is now open on `main` once this lands. The body records it and names #34868 as the carrier. Land #34868 close behind.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
None new.

Next: o3-E lands once the three aggregates are green. #34868 follows to close the skill-versus-tool window. No seat L2 is owed.
